1 FACULTY SENATE OFFICE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE April 15, 2021 Faculty Senate Curriculum and Standards Committee Report 2020-2021-9 At the April 8, 2021 meeting of the Curriculum and Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate.
SECTION I Informational Matters COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: CCJ 280, Introduction to Policing Create online version (3 crs.) Examines the development and history of policing as an institution.
Other topics include police functions, legal issues, the role of discretion, use of force and accountability, and current policing issues. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: CCJ major, C or better in CCJ/PSC 274, or permission of instructor.
COM 422, Communication and Conflict Intervention Create accelerated online version (3 crs.) An examination of the role of communication theories in conflict intervention in interpersonal, group, and organizational settings.
Emphasis on applying theories through simulations, role plays, case studies, and discussions. (Accelerated Online Program) Pre: COM 221 or COM 251 and junior standing in a degree-granting college or permission of instructor.

ENG 260, Women and Literature Create online version (4 crs.) Critical study of selected topics. (Lec. 3, Project 3/Online) (A3) (B1) ENG 263, Introduction to Literary Genres: The Poem Create online version (4 crs.) Introduction to the study of the poem. (Lec. 3, Project 3/Online) (A3) (B1) COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: ACC 202, Managerial Accounting Create online version (3 crs.) Basic techniques and systems used by management accountants in budgeting, cost accounting, cost analysis, and control. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: ACC (BUS) 201 or 201H or permission of instructor.
MGT 445, Strategic Management Create online version (3 crs.) Case studies, simulation or company analysis used to study strategic theory and practice and problems of functional integration in domestic and global firms. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: ACC (BUS) 202 and FIN (BUS) 220 or 220H and MGT (BUS) 341 or 341H and SCA 255 (355) and MKT (BUS) 265 (365) or 265H (365H) and INE 315 or MGT 345, and senior standing in the College of Business, or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit. (D1)

2 COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: BPS 201, How Drugs Work Create online version (3 crs.) Drug actions, uses, and adverse effects of prescription and non-prescription medications, recreational drugs, and nutritional supplements.
General audience. (Lec. 3/Online) Open to all students except health science and related majors. (A1) HONORS PROGRAM: HPR and H-sections Change prerequisites Add to all HPR and H-section courses prerequisites, the student group of THPR for transfer students to be allowed to register for honors courses.
This change is a behind-the-scenes change and not reflected in the course description prerequisite listing.
SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate COURSES CHANGES: COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: ART 105, Motion Graphic Design Change title (3 crs.) Introduction to 4D (time-based) digital design projects for on-line display, live performances, and installations with focus on the production of digital forms of animation, video, photo, sound, and interactivity. (Lec. 1, Studio 2) (A4) ENG/GWS 388, Queer Literatures, Queer Cultures Change course number, cross-list with GWS (4 crs.) Cross-list with (ENG), GWS 388.

Study of queer cultural productions, literature, and related theory, with a focus on historical, aesthetic, and political developments in ongoing contestations around the representations of gender, sexuality, and identity. (Lec. 3, Project 3) (A3) (C3) COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: ACC 404, Auditing Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Auditing standards, procedures, programs, working papers, and internal control. (Lec. 3) Pre: ACC (BUS) 302 or concurrent enrollment in 302, or permission of instructor.
BAI 210, Managerial Statistics I Change prerequisites (3 crs.) General statistical methods used in the collection, presentation, analysis, and interpretation of statistical data.
Includes frequency distribution, measures of central tendency and dispersion, probability theory, sampling distribution, central limit theorem, law of large numbers, estimation, and tests of hypothesis.
Pre: Minimum of C- in BAI 111 or MTH 131 or MTH 141.
BAI 356, Business Analytics Programming Change title, prerequisites (3 crs.) Techniques for business data analytics and visualization using appropriate software platforms (i.e.
R) and real-world business data.

Emphasis on business analytics, handling real-world business data and issues. (Lec. 3) Pre: BAI (BUS) 113.
BAI 456, Database Management Change title, description, prerequisites (3 crs.) Modern concepts and methods in management of large volume of data; creation, design, and implementation

3 of data models, integrity and security.
Use of database management systems (e.g.
RDBMS/NoSQL). (Lec. 3) Pre: Junior standing in a degree-granting college.
CSC 201 or 211 for Data Science major.
BAI 310, Business Data Analysis with Excel Change title, description, prereq, add online version (3 crs.) Introduces intermediate and advanced spreadsheet concepts for business applications.
Import, organize, and evaluate data; apply quantitative analysis and modeling tools to extract meaningful information; communicate results for business decision-making. (Le., 3/Online) Pre: BAI 113 or BAI 111 or equivalent SCA 255, 360,361, 415, 460, 462, 463, and 464 Change prerequisites SCA 359 Change description and prerequisites MKT 465, 466, 467, and 486 Change prerequisites COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES/COLLEGE OF EDUCATION & PROF.
STUDIES: HDF 420 / EDC 421, Early Language and Literacy Development (Birth-5) Change prerequisites, cross-list with EDC 421. (3 crs.) Cross list as (HDF 420), EDC 421.
Theoretical foundations of language and literacy development from birth through age 5.

Examines practical applications of multi-modal language and literacy in diverse populations, including dual language learners. (Lec. 3) Pre: For HDF: HDF200 and either HDF 202 or PSY 301; For ECE: admission into the Early Childhood Education Teacher Certification Program; or permission of instructor.
COLLEGE OF ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: AVS 304, Advanced Animal Management Techniques Change credits (2 to 3) & description Hands-on course in advanced animal handling and management skills needed to maintain animal health and productivity.
Students will use software currently used in the animal industry.
Fields trips required. (Lec. 1, Lab. 1, Rec. 1) Pre: AVS 101 and AVS 102 and either AVS 323 or AVS 324.
COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: BPS 206, Foundations of Cannabis Studies Change prerequisites (3 crs.) The history, regulation, and ethics related to cannabis use are explored.
The endocannabinoid system and cannabinoid pharmacology are introduced. (Accelerated Online Program) Pre: open to students in the cannabis studies certificate program or by permission of program director.

NEW COURSES: COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: APG 345, Introduction to Medical Anthropology (3 crs.) Overview of the perspectives, theories, and methods used by contemporary medical anthropologists.
Cross cultural approach to human health and disease with emphasis on biological, ecological, political, economic, and cultural factors. (Online)

4 APG/SOC 377, Undergraduate Teaching Experience in Anthro/Soc (1-3 crs.) Cross-listed as (APG), SOC 377.
Introduces students to various aspects of college level teaching while working under the supervision of course instructors and/or faculty members in Anthropology or Sociology. (Practicum) Not for major credit.
May be repeated for a maximum of 4 credits.
Pre: permission of instructor.
S/U only.
COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: BAI 494, Business Internship/Field Experience (0 crs.) Undergraduate Business majors completing approved Off Campus Experience.
Fall, Spring, Summer, or Winter Semester.
Registration is by permission number only. (Practicum) Pre: Business major and instructor consent.
Not for graduate credit.
S/U only.
COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES AND UCAS: CSV/SUS 306, Sustainability & Service Leadership (3 crs.) Cross-listed as (CSV), SUS 306.
Students will learn to identify and examine critical sustainability issues and develop communication skills, campaigns, and peer education events that lead to behavior change and a shift in campus culture. (Practicum 2, Online 1/Online) Pre: junior standing.

UNIVERSITY COLLEGE FOR ACADEMIC SUCCESS: CSV 400, Community Based Field Experience (0 crs.) Undergraduate students completing approved community based Field Experience for zero credit.
Fall, Spring, Summer, and Winter J Semester.
Minimum 40 hours field experience.
Registration by permission number only.
S/U only.
ITR 400, Off Campus Field Experience/Internship (0 crs.) Undergraduate students completing approved off-campus Field Experience or Internship for zero credit.
Fall, Spring, Summer Semester.
Minimum 40 hours field experience.
Registration by permission number only.
S/U only.
COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: CVE 472, Biosystems in Environmental Engineering (3 crs.) Microorganisms that constitute the biological systems in environmental engineering processes.
Application of principles of microbiology and biochemistry to analysis and design in fields of environmental engineering and other related fields. (Lec. 3) Pre: Senior level engineering student.
COLLEGE OF ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: BIO 331, Parasitology (currently an X course) (3 crs.) An introduction to the biology of parasitic organisms, including life cycles, infection pathways, and impacts on hosts.

Topics are explored via lecture, laboratory exercises, literature review, and discussion groups. (Lec. 2 Lab. 1) Pre: BIO 101 and BIO 102.
CMB 420, Microbiomes, Biofilms and Bacterial Communities (currently an X course) (3 crs.) A study of bacterial microbiomes and their interaction with hosts and/or their environment.
Emphasis
5 will be placed on attached bacterial communities in environmental and disease contexts. (Lec. 3) Pre: Either CMB 201 or CMB 211, or graduate standing with instructor permission.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) Since its founding in the 1970’s, the mission of the Master of Public Administration (MPA) program at the University of Rhode Island is to instill public values, knowledge, and expertise to

2 prepare our graduates to solve problems related to governance, nonprofit management, and policy with integrity, professionalism, and excellence to improve our communities and society.
To train our students to meet the challenges of the 21st Century, the MPA program is embarking on a series of program revisions and a transition to a fully online program to meet the current and anticipated future needs from employers and various stakeholders across Rhode Island, the region, and nationally.
Although the MPA program will transition to a fully online, accelerated (7-week) format and replace its current blended, 14-week modality, the MPA program will retain many of its successful core features, including the requirement that MPA graduates earn 36 credits.
The accelerated online MPA program also incorporates new curricular innovations that will expand student recruitment and student flexibility.
Additionally, the programmatic and curricular revisions outlined in this proposal are critical for the program to become accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA) – a long-standing goal of the program – in the coming years.

One of the structural revisions and innovations of the online MPA program is the creation of three certificate programs that offer students with both core training in public administration and policy but also specializations mirroring the Public Management and Policy Analysis concentrations in the current program.
The three 12-credit graduate certificates in the online MPA program are: the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, Public Management, and Policy Analysis.
Students in the online MPA program will need to complete the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy graduate certificate, at least one of the other two MPA graduate certificates, earn at least 36 credits, and complete the capstone course to complete their MPA degree.
The core certificate that forms the basis for the MPA online program is the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy.

Students completing this certificate program will have an opportunity to learn about the historical and theoretical foundations of public administration and policy (PSC 501), ethical decision-making strategies (PSC 504), diversity and inclusion in the public sector (PSC 502), and an elective course focused on developing core skills or experience for a career in government, non-profits, or policy.
All students who want to earn their MPA degree will be required to complete this graduate certificate.
In addition to the certificate in Public Administration and Policy, students choosing to graduate with an MPA degree can choose to complete either one or two additional MPA-offered certificates that form the basis of an added credential or specialization that will make graduates competitive in the job market.
The first is a certificate in Public Management.
The coursework required for this certificate will help students become competitive applicants for positions requiring financial and budgetary expertise (PSC 506 & PSC 507), leadership skills, knowledge of administrative law and procedure (PSC 573), and the management of agency personnel (PSC 503).

Currently, there is an acute need in many cities and towns for Finance Director positions, which can be a town or city’s highest paid municipal position.
Additionally, these are skills increasingly

3 sought by nonprofit organizations. By creating a certificate program, we hope to fulfill this workforce need in the state of Rhode Island and beyond by offering incumbent employees and new students the opportunity to develop a competency in Public Management. Our aim is to have incumbent workers trained so that they will have opportunities for advancement, and their advancement will, in turn, create entry-level opportunities for others pursuing a certificate in Public Management or our students completing the MPA program. The second of these optional certificates is the Policy Analysis certificate. The coursework required for this certificate will help students develop research and analytical capabilities (PSC 583 & PSC 510), evaluate public programs (PSC 505), and navigate the public policy process (PSC 524 & PSC 510). These skills will allow them to become effective at shaping public policy either within public agencies or as part of a broader policymaking process. Students pursuing this certificate will develop skills that will allow them to be policy advocates, policy researchers, and/or communication specialists. The underlying philosophy of the URI MPA online program is that its modular design will guide students along pathways that will allow them to align their graduate study with their career ambitions. MPA graduates will have earned no less than 36 credits while completing the program. The design of the MPA online program is not only aligned with NASPAA accreditation guidelines but also meets the growing workplace needs in Rhode Island, the region, and nationally.
To gauge the current and future hiring needs of employers in the public and nonprofit sectors, the MPA director, Dr.
Aaron Ley, conducted a series of meetings with key government and nonprofit stakeholders throughout the state over the last two years.
The meetings included the Rhode Island League of Cities and Towns, the Rhode Island City and Town Managers Association, and various other state agencies like the Rhode Island Secretary of State’s office, among others.

These meetings revealed the growing need of individuals with management and finance backgrounds because employees currently holding these positions are beginning to reach the age of retirement.
These discussions were confirmed through the Director’s own anecdotal experience in Bristol where the town’s finance director chose to take a position closer to home.
During that hiring process for the replacement, the town observed that very few people in its applicant pool were qualified to fill this position.
Nationally, municipal Finance Director positions are among some of the highest paid municipal employees.
In order to address this workforce need, and as part of our migration of the MPA program to an online format, we are proposing the development of a stackable Public Management Certificate that will allow our students to enter our program in order to develop skills relating to public budgeting and finance.

This will allow incumbent workers and entry-level workers to quickly earn a competency in public management by completing a suite of four courses to fulfill this certificate, while also giving them the option of remaining in the program to complete the MPA Online program by completing the other 24 credits.
We hope that the training of incumbent workers will create opportunities for their advancement, which will create entry-level opportunities for others pursuing a certificate in Public Management or our students completing the MPA program.
This stackable certificate can be used by MPA students desiring a special competency in the area of public management, or for students in other graduate programs wanting to use their remaining electives to gain public management skills.

Currently, while there are no data regarding salaries for employees earning certificates, there is extensive survey research that exists on salaries of alumni holding an MPA/MPP degree.
According to a 2018 survey administered by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA), over half of all graduates surveyed with an MPA made over $65,000 after three years of having earned the degree (https://www.naspaa.org/data-center/alumni-survey).
